title: N-th Tribonacci Number
description: Brute force to optimized: plain unmemoized recursion versus three rolling variables sliding forward.

blocks.text: Problem Summary: The Tribonacci sequence is defined by T0 = 0, T1 = 1, T2 = 1, and Tn = T(n-1) + T(n-2) + T(n-3) for n greater than or equal to 3. Given n, return the value of Tn.

blocks.caption: What goes in, what comes out

blocks.text: This is a direct generalization of the Fibonacci recurrence: instead of summing the two immediately preceding terms, sum the THREE immediately preceding terms. Once the three base cases (T0, T1, T2) are known, every later term follows mechanically.

blocks.title: Analogy: A Savings Account That Adds the Last Three Months' Deposits Together
blocks.text: Picture a peculiar savings rule where this month's deposit equals the sum of the deposits made in the three previous months. Once the first three months are known, every later month's deposit follows automatically by summing the three before it.

blocks.caption: Each term is the sum of the three immediately preceding terms

blocks.title: Building the Intuition
blocks.text:
Observation 1: The three base cases T0=0, T1=1, T2=1 are given directly, no computation needed.

Observation 2: For n>=3, Tn depends ONLY on the three immediately preceding values, none further back.

Observation 3: Since only the last three values are ever needed at any point, there is no need to store the entire sequence, just three rolling variables that slide forward one step at a time.
This leads to tracking just three rolling variables, updating them one step at a time until reaching n.
Compute Tn via plain recursion, directly calling T(n-1), T(n-2), and T(n-3), without memoization.
Why the code is written this way

items: Direct recursion following the recurrence definition is the simplest implementation.
This recomputes the same smaller values repeatedly across different branches, costing exponential time; tracking just the last three values with rolling variables avoids all repeated work.

blocks.title: Time and Space Complexity
blocks.text:
Time: O(3 raised to n) without memoization.
Space: O(n) recursion depth.
Limitation: since only the last three values are ever needed, three rolling variables computed bottom-up avoid all repeated recursive calls.

blocks.title: The Optimization Journey
blocks.text: Handle the base cases (n=0 returns 0, n=1 or n=2 returns 1) directly. Otherwise, maintain three rolling variables a, b, c representing T(i-3), T(i-2), T(i-1) as i advances from 3 to n; at each step, compute the next value as a+b+c, then shift all three variables forward by one position. After reaching n, c holds the answer.
Use three rolling variables, sliding forward one step at a time until reaching n.

Since Tn depends only on the three immediately preceding values, maintaining exactly those three values and sliding them forward one step at a time correctly reconstructs the sequence up to n, without ever needing to store the full history or repeat any computation.

blocks.title: If The Interviewer Says This, Think This
blocks.text: If the interviewer says "each term is the sum of a fixed number of preceding terms", think: rolling variables tracking exactly that many prior values.

blocks.title: Complexity Summary
blocks.text: The unmemoized recursive approach costs O(3^n); the rolling-variable approach costs O(n), the standard efficient solution.

items: Pattern: rolling variables tracking a fixed window of preceding terms.
Core Idea: Tn = T(n-1) + T(n-2) + T(n-3), directly generalizing the Fibonacci recurrence.
Time: O(3^n) for the brute force, O(n) for the rolling-variable approach.
Space: O(n) recursion depth for the brute force, O(1) extra for the rolling-variable approach.
Most Important Observation: only the last three values ever matter at any point.
Interview Difficulty: a foundational, easy 1D DP problem.
One line memory trick: sum the last three, then slide the window.
